key_insight: PANY enables 6D pose estimation for unseen objects without needing CAD models, making it possible to localize objects from arbitrary reference views even when overlap is low or the object is heavily occluded. It unifies RGB and RGB-D inputs in a model-free framework.
problem_solved: The paper addresses open-world 6D object pose estimation for unseen objects, especially the failure of existing model-free methods when query-reference overlap is small, viewpoints change dramatically, or occlusions are present.
method: Introduces PANY, a unified model-free pose estimation framework that works with both RGB and RGB-D inputs.
Moves beyond pairwise single-anchor matching by supporting arbitrary reference views for more robust pose inference.
Designed to handle challenging real-world conditions such as occlusion, low overlap, and large viewpoint variation without requiring CAD assets.
impact: This matters because it lowers the barrier to deploying pose estimation in robotics and embodied AI, where objects are often unseen and CAD models are unavailable. Practitioners gain a more flexible and scalable way to estimate object pose in cluttered, real-world environments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing query image + arbitrary reference images feeding into pose prediction

paper_title: Pose Anything Anywhere:Model-free Object Poses from Arbitrary References
paper_authors: Hongli Xu, Jiaqi Hu, Junwen Huang, Boyang Zhong, Peter KT Yu
